Professional profile

Overview of computing, vocational training and curriculum leadership

Computer Science teacher and technical-education leader with more than 20 years’ experience across the UK and Cuba. Currently the sole Computer Science teacher for Years 5–13 at an independent school in West Sussex, including OCR J277 GCSE and H446 A Level. Previous leadership includes seven years directing five Joven Club de Computación y Electrónica (JCCE) centres delivering certified, employment-oriented computing courses. Experienced in curriculum development, practical technical skills, assessment, team management and inclusive education.

Qualifications & professional recognition

Qualified Teacher Status (England), Assessment Only route completed June 2026; certificate pending final programme payment on 27 November 2026.

Early Career Teacher induction ongoing; anticipated completion during the 2026–27 school year.

MSc, New Technologies for Education — ISPJAE/CUJAE, Havana; awarded 9 July 2007. UK ENIC comparison: Master’s degree, RQF Level 7.

BSc, Computer Science with Applied Mathematics — CUJAE, Havana; awarded 15 July 1992. UK ENIC comparison: Bachelor degree, RQF Level 6.

US High School Equivalency Diploma — Georgia, 10 July 1986. Obtained because the previously completed Cuban secondary qualification was not recognised in the United States. UK ENIC: RQF Level 2, comparable to GCSE grades 9–4/A*–C for subjects passed.

University of Havana: Special Teaching Category of Adjunct Instructor, awarded June 2005.

Results & technical capability

2026 OCR GCSE J277: 10 of 13 pupils achieved grades 4–9; five achieved grades 7–9, including one grade 9.

2026 OCR A Level H446: two of three candidates achieved A or B.

Technical teaching: Python, SQL/SQLite, algorithms, networks, computer systems, databases, digital safety, Scratch, App Lab, Google Workspace, Moodle and assessment design.

Professional autobiography

First-person narrative spanning school education, military training, cross-cultural youth programmes, university teaching, vocational leadership and UK Computer Science education.

Note on historical dates: These dates are approximate because the original documentation remains in Cuba and is not currently available. Where no year can be established, the activity is described without assigning a date.

Professional introduction

I am a Computer Science educator and technical-training leader with more than 20 years of experience in teaching, computing provision and educational management. My career has included higher and secondary education, distance learning, certified vocational digital-skills programmes and UK GCSE and A Level Computer Science. My professional interests have consistently centred on helping learners acquire useful knowledge, apply it in practical settings and develop confidence as independent problem-solvers.

School, military training and qualifications

1966–1992 · Original account with reconstructed school dates clearly identified

I attended Hugo Camejo Valdés Primary School in Marianao, Havana, Cuba, from approximately 1966 to 1973, completing kindergarten and Grades 1–6. I then attended José Antonio Aguilera Maceira Secondary School, also in Marianao, from approximately 1973 to 1976, completing Grades 7–9. These dates are approximate because the original documentation remains in Cuba and is not currently available.

I continued my education at Manolito Aguilar High School in Havana, completing Grades 10–13, provisionally dated 1976–1980. After upper-secondary education, I completed three years of military service in Havana, followed by military academy training at the Antonio Maceo Military Academy in Matanzas, Cuba, until 1986. These dates are approximate because the original school and military documentation remains in Cuba and is not currently available.

In 1986, my family relocated to New York, USA. I also obtained a United States High School Equivalency Diploma in Atlanta, Georgia, because my completed Cuban high-school qualification was not recognised for US educational credentialing. The diploma was therefore an additional US-recognised credential, not evidence of incomplete schooling or a second high-school course. My UK ENIC statement compares the subjects passed, including English and Mathematics, with GCSE grades 9–4 / A*–C. Both events occurred in 1986; their precise sequence is not specified here.

I went on to complete a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science with Applied Mathematics at CUJAE in Havana. My degree studies were completed on 15 July 1992, and the diploma was issued on 20 July 1992. UK ENIC has compared this qualification to a UK Bachelor’s degree (RQF Level 6). My university enrolment date is not specified here because the original documentation remains in Cuba and is not currently available.

International youth programmes & cultural learning

Angola → Congo → USSR · Programme dates unavailable

Alongside my formal education and subsequent volunteer work, I accompanied my family on overseas postings related to my father’s work as a Cuban official. Our stays included Angola, Congo and the former Soviet Union (USSR), in that order. During these periods I enrolled in local youth programmes, mainly involving educational support for young people; in some cases, the programmes also helped me learn about the local language and culture. These experiences developed my adaptability, cultural awareness and commitment to educational inclusion. The precise dates and programme records remain in Cuba and are not currently available to me. These were separate youth-programme experiences, not a single continuous appointment or the 1992–1996 Youth for Understanding programme.

Early teaching, volunteering and university recognition

1992–2007 · Some dates approximate; records in Cuba

Following completion of my BSc in 1992, I participated in further youth and early-career development activities during the broader 1992–1996 period. These included Youth for Understanding (YFU), a student exchange programme based in Washington, DC, USA, separate from the overseas family postings described above. Through this experience, I volunteered as a tutor in youth correctional centres and supported a local welfare office serving vulnerable young people. These activities provided practical experience in tutoring, community support and working with learners facing challenging circumstances. My YFU participation falls within the broader 1992–1996 period, although the specific programme dates are unavailable. I also held teaching appointments in Havana before September 2007; dates for these earlier appointments are approximate because the original documentation remains in Cuba and is not currently available.

In June 2005, the University of Havana’s Faculty of Mathematics and Computing awarded me the Special Teaching Category of Adjunct Instructor. In 2007, I completed a Master’s degree in New Technologies for Education at ISPJAE/CUJAE, subsequently compared by UK ENIC to a UK Master’s degree at RQF Level 7. This postgraduate study strengthened my work in educational technology, curriculum planning and digital pedagogy.

Vocational education & management — JCCE

September 2007–August 2014

Following my Master’s degree, I became Municipal Director of five Joven Club de Computación y Electrónica (JCCE) centres in the municipality of La Lisa, Havana. I was responsible for more than 40 staff and programmes serving approximately 1,000 learners every four months. This was a substantial public technical-education leadership position, combining the management of centres and people with oversight of teaching and learner outcomes.

Our centres delivered practical, certificated courses in computer use, programming, database design, graphics, photo editing and network design and administration. A particularly relevant programme was Operador de Microcomputadoras (Microcomputer Operator), an employment-oriented certificate used in Cuba to support access to certain jobs. Published academic research describes this JCCE course as recognised by Cuba’s Ministry of Labour and Social Security. My involvement concerned leadership of the training provision and its associated teaching, assessment and certification processes; I do not claim that this certificate is formally equivalent to a specific UK NVQ, BTEC or T Level.

The centres served school and university students, older adults, disabled learners and individuals experiencing social disadvantage. This broadened my understanding of accessible technical instruction and the importance of matching delivery to diverse learner needs. I also developed an early dynamic website for the programme in Havana Province using PHP-Fusion, and received the organisation’s national Vanguard Worker of the Year award in four consecutive years.

Classroom teaching & university distance education

2014–2017

From September 2014 to June 2015, I worked as a cover teacher with the Havana provincial education service, teaching Computer Science, Mathematics and English to lower-secondary pupils. This role reconnected my technical and leadership background with classroom teaching, lesson planning and responsive assessment. July and August were the normal school summer holiday period between the end of this appointment and the next September academic-year appointment, rather than an unexplained absence from employment.

From September 2015 to June 2017, I was Head of Department for Distance Education at the University of Pedagogical Sciences Enrique José Varona in Havana. I led staff delivering online-learning support and digital education services to more than 200 students, supported colleagues in their use of digital platforms and directed the development of accessible distance-learning provision.

Online tuition & progression into UK schools

2017–2024

In July 2017, I relocated to the United Kingdom and used the initial period to settle and adjust. From August 2017 until September 2023, my recorded professional activity was self-employed online tuition associated with Staff Complete Remote Services in Liverpool. I supported individual learners through tailored explanation, practical tasks and formative feedback. For a formal agency background check, the locations and dates associated with remote employment and physical residence should be verified from immigration, employment and travel records.

In September 2023, I joined Robert Clack School of Science in Dagenham, teaching KS3 computing alongside Mathematics until May 2024. From June to December 2024, I taught at Lancing College in West Sussex, including A Level Computer Science and Mathematics. These appointments deepened my experience of the English curriculum, examination requirements, classroom practice and school assessment expectations.

Current Computer Science teaching

January 2025–present

Since January 2025, I have worked as a Computer Science Teacher at an independent school in West Sussex, delivering the subject across Years 5–13. As the sole subject specialist, I take responsibility for planning, resources, assessment and examination preparation from upper primary through GCSE OCR J277 and A Level OCR H446. My teaching covers Python, algorithms, computer systems, networks, databases and safe, responsible use of digital technology. I also undertake form-tutor and safeguarding responsibilities and previously supported pupils through boarding-house duties.

In the 2026 examinations, 10 of my 13 OCR GCSE candidates achieved grades 4–9, including five grades 7–9 and one grade 9. Two of the three A Level Computer Science candidates achieved an A or B grade. I completed the Assessment Only route to Qualified Teacher Status in June 2026; the certificate was awaiting the final programme payment scheduled for 27 November 2026 at the time this autobiography was prepared. My ECT induction remained ongoing during the 2026–27 academic year.

Professional approach & future contribution

My work across academic and vocational settings has led me to emphasise clear explanation followed by practical application, diagnostic questions, progressively challenging tasks and feedback grounded in transparent success criteria. I have developed digital curriculum and assessment tools, including Project X, to support structured teaching and student independence. I am interested in permanent Computer Science, further education and vocational digital-skills roles where I can combine subject expertise with curriculum improvement, staff support and high-quality technical training.

Personal interests & lifelong learning

Outside my professional responsibilities, I maintain a range of interests that support intellectual curiosity and personal development. I read widely, including in metaphysics, and practise meditation and mindfulness. Physical training and dancing are also important interests. I follow stock-market investing as part of my wider interest in finance and independent learning.

These interests complement my educational work by encouraging reflection, curiosity, personal discipline and an appreciation of different ways of learning.
